mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in housing and manufacturing demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12M MA and INDPRO > 12M MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their 12-month averages indicates a dual shock of inflation and policy tightening, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12M MA and FEDFUNDS > 12M MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (implied by RSAFS falling for four consecutive months) signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces consumer demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
